quick: Intra-articular knee: 1 injection/week x3-5 (product-specific); ophthalmic: 1-2 drops as needed
Limited data; intra-articular use generally avoided unless needed
Minimal systemic absorption; considered low risk
summary: Hyaluronic acid (hyaluronan) is a naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan used as a viscosupplement for knee osteoarthritis, an ophthalmic lubricant for dry eye, a dermal filler, and a component of wound and tissue products. It restores viscoelasticity and lubrication. It acts locally with minimal systemic absorption; the main adverse effects are transient local reactions. Most intra-articular and dermal preparations are regulated as medical devices rather than approved drugs in many regions.
indications: Symptomatic knee osteoarthritis not responsive to conservative therapy and simple analgesics (intra-articular viscosupplementation)
Relief of dry eye / ocular surface lubrication (ophthalmic)
Surgical aid in ophthalmic procedures (ophthalmic viscoelastic device)
Soft-tissue augmentation / correction of facial wrinkles (dermal filler)
Adjunct to wound and mucosal healing (topical/mucosal preparations)

dosage.d: 1 injection into affected knee weekly for 3-5 weeks (product-dependent)
dosage.n: Single-injection cross-linked products also available; repeat course per response

dosage.d: 1-2 drops into affected eye(s) as needed
Inject to correct contour/wrinkle per area
Apply to affected area as directed

admin: Intra-articular injections must be given under aseptic technique by a trained clinician
Aspirate any joint effusion before injecting and avoid intravascular injection
Do not use disinfectants containing quaternary ammonium salts to prep skin (can precipitate hyaluronan)
Avoid strenuous activity or prolonged weight-bearing for ~48 hours after intra-articular injection
Ophthalmic drops: avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye; remove contact lenses if specified
moa: Hyaluronic acid is a high-molecular-weight glycosaminoglycan that is a major component of synovial fluid and the extracellular matrix. As a viscosupplement it restores the viscoelastic and lubricating properties of osteoarthritic synovial fluid, may reduce pain and inflammation, and provides mechanical cushioning. As an ocular/topical agent it forms a hydrating, lubricating film that retains moisture and supports tissue repair.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to hyaluronate preparations (some derived from avian/bacterial sources)
Infection or skin disease at/around the injection site (intra-articular)
relative: Active joint infection or marked joint inflammation
Venous or lymphatic stasis in the limb (intra-articular)
Bleeding disorders or anticoagulation (injection bleeding risk)
monitor: Signs of injection-site infection or inflammatory flare

preg: There are limited data on use during pregnancy. Systemic exposure from local administration is minimal; intra-articular and cosmetic use is generally deferred during pregnancy unless clearly needed.
lact: Systemic absorption from local administration is minimal and excretion into breast milk is not expected to be clinically significant; considered low risk during breastfeeding.
renal: Hyaluronan is degraded locally and in the liver/lymphatics; no renal dose adjustment is required.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment; endogenous hyaluronan is partly cleared by the liver but exogenous local dosing requires no adjustment.

minor: Disinfectants/local anesthetics containing quaternary ammonium salts may precipitate hyaluronan - avoid for skin prep

serious: Acute pseudoseptic reaction / inflammatory flare in the joint
emergency: Vascular occlusion with vision loss or tissue necrosis (filler)

monitoring: Local injection-site reaction and joint effusion after intra-articular use
Signs of joint infection (fever, increasing pain, erythema)
Visual or skin changes after dermal filler (vascular compromise)
counsel: Expect possible mild pain or swelling at the injection site that usually resolves in a few days
Rest the joint and avoid strenuous or prolonged weight-bearing activity for about 48 hours after knee injection
Report increasing joint pain, swelling, redness or fever promptly
For eye drops, do not let the tip touch the eye; mild brief blurring may occur
Tell your clinician about any allergy to these products before treatment
pk: Symptom relief over days to weeks (viscosupplement)
Maximal OA benefit typically several weeks after a course
Local residence ~hours to days; rapidly degraded
OA benefit may last up to ~6 months
Refrigerate or store per product (often 2-8 C or controlled room temp); do not freeze
pearls: NOTE: Intra-articular and dermal hyaluronic acid products are largely regulated as medical devices, not FDA-approved drugs; dosing is product-specific (refer to the individual product's instructions for use)
Acts locally with negligible systemic absorption - hence few systemic contraindications or interactions
Avoid quaternary-ammonium skin disinfectants which precipitate hyaluronan
Aspirate joint effusion before viscosupplement injection and use strict aseptic technique
Dermal filler vascular occlusion is a true emergency - hyaluronidase reverses HA fillers
missed: For a scheduled intra-articular injection course, reschedule a missed injection with the clinician to complete the planned series. For ophthalmic/topical use, simply resume the regular schedule; doubling is unnecessary.
overdose: Systemic overdose is not expected due to local administration and rapid degradation. Excess local product may cause transient swelling or discomfort; manage symptomatically. For dermal filler complications (vascular occlusion), hyaluronidase can dissolve hyaluronic acid filler.
